coaching.headline: Four lane reads said unfavored and the players beat every one of them — eight won fights, six cashed, and 94,158 objective damage to their 6,253.
coaching.team: The early film matched the bad reads — Grux was down three deaths by 9.2 and the 6.1 fight was taken with both losing lanes pinned — and then the team simply stopped trading and started converting: 2-0 at our Fangtooth at 9.8, 3-1 at Mini Prime at 17.6, and every won fight after that fed the ledger until Fangtooth three times over, Mini Prime, Genesis Core, Orb Prime and Primal Fangtooth were all banked by 32. They won exactly one fight all game. This is what fighting on top of our own objectives looks like.
coaching.whatShiftedIt: The 3-1 at our Mini Prime at 17.6 — won by Legion and Grux standing two against four — turned a scrappy laning phase into the rolling objective train that finished 23-16 in takes and 8-2 in towers.

perPlayer.7c8ab99c-31c5-4ea5-a6fa-e0d6417c3f1b: Mr_Meat31's Legion was read 'theirs all game' against Howitzer and won it anyway — 8/4/8 with early kills on Howitzer at 6.8 and 8.9, the solo 2-0 at our Fangtooth at 9.8, and half of the two-man Mini Prime stand at 17.6. Beating an immobile zone mage by refusing to sit in his zones is the textbook play, executed.
perPlayer.16f28434-561f-4f23-9454-40321f4a1ef3: Goldilocks324 ate three deaths before 9.2 — including the 3.6 solo catch by Bayle — then flipped the offlane completely: Shinbi died to Grux six times, and 25,300 objective damage came with it. The one open item note is no magic resist into a four-magical comp; the comeback covered for it this time.
perPlayer.a0c393cc-1437-4bdc-8168-64676ce2166c: Cuban Noobster's Serath opened with first blood at 2.5 and finished as the objective engine of the match — 58,130 objective damage, the most on either team, on an 8/3/6 line. The jungle read said 'theirs all game'; the map disagreed by minute 10.
perPlayer.10edbf65-457d-48d0-9151-9df5b4fcb40a: Willy Guggenheim's Steel was flawless where it counts: 5/0/11, zero deaths, 48,227 mitigated and a game-high 17 wards. Dekker died to him three times in the support matchup, and the peel is why Legion and Serath could keep diving.
perPlayer.a412baf3-dd17-4f89-8ecf-9d0704f3a79e: Xeebs played the quiet mid game — 4/2/4 into an even-then-losing read against Neon — and showed up where it decided things: the solo 2-0 defending our Orb Prime at 30.1 and two more kills in the closing 32.5-to-32.9 fight at their outer tower. Holding the Orb Prime pit alone against two is the play of his game.

threats: Chain-CC risk (2 hard-CC abilities, ~1.0s of lockdown): Howitzer Land Mine (knockback), Bayle Kingslayer (knockback). Don't group tight into it — stagger the engage and hold mobility/cleanse for the key one.
Enemy is 4/5 magical — one magic-resist item goes a long way.
synergy: Our engage/CC: Grux Crush (knockup 0.5s). Our kills come from landing burst INSIDE that CC window — whoever lands it, the rest must follow up immediately.
We have sustain (Steel) — favor the longer fight where our heals out-grind them.
Strong AoE/teamfight kit — group at choke points and fight on top of objectives.

ourKits.combo: Smash 'n Grab pull → Crush knockup → Warlord's Challenge stun → bleed-stacked basics
ourKits.winCondition: land the pull→knockup chain to lock a target while bleed and AS shred them
ourKits.passive: basics stack a bleed for sustained damage
ourKits.playWith: follow-up burst inside his knockup/stun window
ourKits.playAgainst: telegraphed engage — bait Crush/Pull, then punish; kite his slow start

ourKits.combo: Ascend dive → Heaven's Fury multi-strike → Chastise slow → Heresy form ult, resets on takedowns
ourKits.winCondition: dive the backline and snowball Heresy resets
ourKits.playWith: a frontline that creates her dive angle
ourKits.playAgainst: peel the backline — deny the first kill and her resets dry up

ourKits.combo: Bull Rush knockback → Force Shield wall → Shield Slam knockup+stun ult, Shield Bash %hp
ourKits.winCondition: peel the carry with walls/knockups or engage with Shield Slam
ourKits.playWith: a carry he can wall for and peel
ourKits.playAgainst: his Force Shield blocks projectiles — reposition around it; bait Shield Slam

ourKits.combo: Soulfire waves → Mortal Coil pull-zone → Stupor orb → Abyssal Rift zone
ourKits.winCondition: zone a fight with Mortal Coil + ult and chunk from range
ourKits.passive: consumes essences from kills for power
ourKits.playWith: frontline to hold enemies in her zones
ourKits.playAgainst: fragile and reliant on her zones — flank/dive around the telegraphs

enemyKits.combo: Slow Grenades / Land Mine zone → R2000 Missile → Make It Rain ult
enemyKits.winCondition: wall off space with mines/grenades and rain artillery on a held enemy
enemyKits.playWith: CC and chokes that force enemies into his zones
enemyKits.playAgainst: immobile turret — flank his mine zones, dive when ult is down

enemyKits.combo: Skull Crusher gap-close → Dire Howl slow → Cursed Edge → Kingslayer knockback dash, Berserk at low HP
enemyKits.winCondition: engage, drop low into Berserk and out-brawl
enemyKits.playWith: follow-up while he commits the dive
enemyKits.playAgainst: his Berserk rewards low HP — burst him fully or disengage; anti-heal helps

enemyKits.combo: Rushing Beat dashes → Line Tempo wolves → Circle Rhythm shield → All-Kill! wolfpack ult
enemyKits.winCondition: stack Track and unleash All-Kill! in a grouped fight
enemyKits.playAgainst: spread vs the wolfpack; she's squishy without her shield up

enemyKits.combo: Stasis Bomb stun → Photon Disruptor slow → Containment Fence wall → Ion Strike slow ult
enemyKits.winCondition: lock a target with stun + fence and let the team collapse
enemyKits.passive: Rocket Boots mobility, refreshed by abilities
enemyKits.playWith: burst that converts her stun/fence into a kill
enemyKits.playAgainst: dodge Stasis Bomb; the fence zones — flank around it

loadout.name: Ferocity
loadout.text: Gain 1% Total Attack Speed per 1s in Hero Combat, stacking infinitely.
loadout.plain: Your attack speed keeps climbing every second you stay in a hero fight. Rewards long fights where Legion can keep shooting from safety.

Stack (Kept alive in fights): 4 effects on one trigger: Malady, Deathstalker, The Perforator, Savage Strikes. Together they made staying in a long fight cheaper: more armor, shields or healing the longer it went.
Stack (Every basic attack set off): 3 effects on one trigger: Deathstalker, Thraex, Savage Strikes.

Stack (Every ability hit set off): 2 effects on one trigger: Tainted Trident, The Perforator. Legion has 4 damaging abilities (Frag Order, Saturation Charge, Rally Point hit an area, so one cast sets them off on several heroes), and 71 ability haste brought them back 42% sooner: more casts, more triggers.

The Eternal was part of it: Thraex (Savage Strikes + Ferocity) sits on the same triggers as the items (kept alive in fights; every basic attack set off), so the same fights paid out in both damage and staying power.
Countered? 0 of the 4 players Legion killed built physical armor. Anti-heal on Bayle, Shinbi, Dekker. We killed Legion 4 times.

Copy it? Thraex (Savage Strikes + Ferocity): 50% in 410 Legion carry games, below the hero's 52.5%; this 3-item core: 54.2% in 1,433 games, below the 57.1% of that hero-role's cores. It wins less than usual elsewhere: it beat us, not the field.

copy.text: Krix (Regenerative Tissue + Cannibalism): 51.9% in 8,915 Steel support games, level with the hero's 51.7%; this 3-item core: 52.2% in 136 games, below the 58.4% of that hero-role's cores. It wins less than usual elsewhere: it beat us, not the field.

loadout.name: Heavy Metal
loadout.text: Heavy Punches and Shield Bash deal Bonus Magical Damage On-Hit equal to 10% of your Total Physical Armor and Magical Armor.

ability.name: Shield Bash
ability.what: Swipe forward with Steel's shield, dealing 35/65/95/125/155 (+50%) (+5/5.75/6.5/7.25/8% of the Target's maximum health) magical damage to all Enemies in front of him and Stunning them for 0.5s.

loadout.plain: Heavy punches and Shield Bash deal extra magic damage based on his armor, so the tankier Steel builds, the harder they hit. Alternate attacks to reach the heavy punch.

loadout.name: Krix
loadout.text: Gain 5% (+1% per Level) increased Maximum Health, and bonus size equal to 0.5% of your Maximum Health.
loadout.plain: Plain bonus maximum health that grows each level. It also makes his passive Cybernetic Shell shield bigger, since that shield scales with his max health.

loadout.name: Regenerative Tissue
loadout.text: After 8s without taking Hero damage, regenerate 0.2/0.4/0.7/1% Max Health per second at Levels 1/6/11/16.
loadout.plain: After 8s without hero damage he slowly regenerates health. Safe recovery between lane trades without going back to base.

loadout.name: Cannibalism
loadout.text: Takedowns permanently increase your Maximum Health by 25.
loadout.plain: Each takedown permanently adds a little max health, which also grows his passive shield. Generic tankiness otherwise.

loadout.name: Sanctification
loadout.text: Safeguard:  Grants yourself and nearby Heroes a 150 (+8%) Shield for 3s. While the Shield holds, Heroes gain 50% Tenacity. Visionary:  Gain Solstone. Increase Ward Cap from 2 to 3. Pacifist:  Receive diminishing Gold from Minion kills.
loadout.plain: Shields Steel and nearby allies, and while the shield holds, stuns and slows on them wear off faster. Pop it as he Bull Rushes in so the team follows safely. Also adds an extra ward.

lead.title: Hard to kill
lead.text: Never died in 33 minutes, fewer deaths than about 95% of Steel support players this patch. The build added health and armor and healing off damage. It came from the Eternal setup (Krix, Regenerative Tissue, Cannibalism) plus Heavy Metal, Sanctification, Raiment of Renewal.
